record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Elementary proof for the p=1 constant-function criterion
record.original_question: Find a more direct and elementary proof, in the spirit of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung, of the p=1 case of the theorem asserting that if a measurable u satisfies λΦ_{λ,p}(u)→0 as λ→∞, then u is constant, where Φ_{λ,p}(u) is the measure of pairs (x,y) for which |u(x)-u(y)|^p/|x-y|^{p+N} ≥ λ.

evidence.quote: Theorem 9.1 is due to Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung [BVY] when p > 1, (with Ω = RN but the proof is unchanged when Ω is a ball), and to Poliakovsky [Pol, Corollary 1.1] when p = 1. Actually, Poliakovsky derives the result from a deeper assertion (see below); as a consequence the proof of Theorem 9.1 when p = 1 is quite intricate and it would be desirable to find a more direct and elementary proof, possibly in the spirit of [BVY].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 1$ and, for a measurable function $u:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}$ (or on a ball $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$), $p\ge 1$, and $\lambda>0$, define
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\;=\;\Big|\Big\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega:\;\frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{p+N}}\ \ge\ \lambda\Big\}\Big|,$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes the $2N$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. It is known that if
$$\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\;=\;0,$$
then $u$ is constant almost everywhere. For $p>1$ this admits a direct proof in the style of Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung (using simple covering/rearrangement arguments). For $p=1$, the only known proof is indirect, going through a substantially deeper statement.

Problem: Provide a direct, elementary proof of the $p=1$ case — i.e. show, by arguments in the spirit of the $p>1$ proof of Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung and without appealing to the deeper machinery, that any measurable $u$ satisfying $\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,1}(u)\to 0$ as $\lambda\to\infty$ is almost everywhere constant.
artifact.status_search_result: The p=1 case is known (proved by Poliakovsky as a corollary of a deeper result), but the request for an elementary, direct proof in the spirit of Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung does not appear to be addressed in the literature found. Related elementary approaches (e.g. via Vitali covering) cover 1≤p<∞ for related characterizations but reportedly break down at p=1 in the relevant range. No source confirming a direct elementary proof for this specific Φ_{λ,1} statement was located.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on a formula for Sobolev norms due to Brezis, Van Schaftingen and Yung
status_evidence.snippet: Poliakovsky provides answers to questions raised by Brezis, Van Schaftingen and Yung, including the p=1/weak-L^q case via a deeper assertion.
status_evidence.claim: The p=1 case was settled by Poliakovsky via a deeper assertion, not by a direct elementary argument.

status_evidence.title: Anisotropic versions of the Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung approach at s=1 and s=0
status_evidence.snippet: Approach based on Vitali covering lemma works for 1≤p<∞ but breaks down at p=1 in the relevant range.
status_evidence.claim: Standard elementary covering-based proofs break down at p=1.

status_evidence.title: Analysis & PDE Vol. 17 No. 3 (2024), Brezis–Seeger–Van Schaftingen–Yung
status_evidence.snippet: For p=1 upper bounds for L^{1,∞} quasinorms fail in certain ranges; the p=1 case exhibits distinct phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: The p=1 regime remains qualitatively different and delicate.
